we propose TD- VAEs, a generative model that learns representations of future states, which are then used to perform planning, and show that it outperforms baselines on a range of planning problems, both simulated and real.

TD-VAE (a) can generate sequences of images that are temporally coherent, (b) can be trained on a large variety of datasets, including images of moving cars, and (c) can be used as a generative model for reinforcement learning.

we propose an approach to model the dynamics of a system by training a variational auto-encoder on pairs of temporaly separated time points using temporal difference learning, and that this approach is able to model the dynamics and uncertainty in the dynamics of the system, and to perform long term planning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning representations of complex environments that allow for efficient planning and control.
the development of a generative model that can be rolled forward in time and that can be used for planning.
the problem of learning to simulate the world in order to act and plan in it.

TD-VAEs are a promising new tool in the field of reinforcement learning, but they are not yet ready to be used in real applications, and there is still some work to do before they can be used as an alternative to other existing techniques.
TD-VAE can learn to predict the future in a way that is more temporally abstract and less uncertain than other generative sequence models.
TD-VAE can be used for generating sequences, and for planning in the sense of predicting the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a new model that learns to predict the future and that learns to plan, in an end-to-end fashion, using only a single loss function, and no hand-designed components.
we propose a generative model that learns representations with explicit uncertainty about future states and can be used for planning in continuous state-action spaces.
TD-VAE can generate sequences of images, and that it can be used to generate a sequence of beliefs about the world that can be used for planning.
The main takeaway from our work is that

temporal difference learning, which is a core component of reinforcement learning, can be used as a training objective for generative models, and that it enables learning of a model that is able to perform temporal abstraction.
the TD-VAE architecture can learn representations of the world that are useful for planning, even when the training objective is not explicitly planning-related.
the TD-VAE model is able to learn a representation that is predictive of future states, while at the same time being able to represent uncertainty about the future.
